SKIP-NOT-HALT: the run never stops for a question. A card that cannot proceed gets its question field filled with the structured decision-needed text (DECISION NEEDED, CONTEXT, OPTIONS, RECOMMENDATION, IMPACT IF UNANSWERED), blocked_on set to the person who owes the answer, status set to blocked, and the executor moves to the next eligible card in the same session. A recommendation is mandatory: a question without one is unfinished. DEFAULTS: every card carries a defaults field holding the pre-authorized answers to that card's expected ambiguities. When defaults covers an ambiguity the executor applies it and logs the application in notes, and does not ask. Defaults fill silence, they never override an explicit instruction in the card. ACCEPTANCE: every card names a machine-checkable acceptance line, a command with an expected exit code, a URL with expected content, or a named test. No acceptance, no ship. A card whose acceptance cannot be run yet is blocked, never shipped. MIGRATIONS: authored as supabase/migrations/NNNN_name.sql files, listed in the PR description by path, and applied by Ivan alone in the Supabase SQL editor. No terminal in this repo ever connects to a database. A card whose acceptance needs an APPLIED migration is set blocked_on ivan with the apply request written into question. A migration file is never edited after it has been applied; a correction is a new numbered file. SECRETS: environment variable names only. Values never appear in chat, in this board, in a commit, in a log or in tool output. /Users/ivan/rc-secrets is out of bounds for reads. ELIGIBILITY: a card is eligible when status is todo, every id in depends_on belongs to a shipped card, and blocked_on is null. The executor takes the lowest-id eligible card. cards.defaults: UNITS: the unit enum is the phase 1 mock set, m2, lm, pcs, bag, kg, roll, m3, and nothing else. The stored enum values are those English tokens; the Romanian display labels the phase 1 UI already uses (m2, lm, buc, sac, kg, rola, m3) stay in the presentation layer as a lookup, because UI copy is Romanian and stored enum values are not UI copy. CURRENCY: the currency enum is EUR, RON, MDL. No FX rates and no runtime conversion; a stored total in a stored currency, exactly as phase 1 did it. NAMING: snake_case for every table, column, enum, index and constraint. Tables plural, columns singular, foreign keys named <referenced_table_singular>_id, timestamps created_at and updated_at, primary keys uuid with gen_random_uuid(). Read policies are to authenticated only; write policies are role-checked against profiles.role. cards.notes:
The foundation card. Authors ONE SQL file and nothing else: no client, no queries, no screens. Tables: products, categories, units, inbound_orders, order_lines, batches, outbound_issues, outbound_lines, status_history, reminders, profiles. profiles carries the role enum with exactly two values, owner and account_manager, and is keyed on the Supabase auth.users id. RLS is ENABLED on every one of those tables, with authenticated-only read policies and role-checked write policies. A table without RLS enabled is the defect this card exists to prevent, so the file ends with an explicit ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY line per table, grouped and commented, so a reader can count them against the table list. Stock is NOT a column. Stock is the sum of a product's batches, per the P2-04 default, so no products.stock column is created here. NO TERMINAL CONNECTS TO A DATABASE. This card produces a file. EXIT STATE, DISCHARGED 2026-08-25: this card originally ended blocked_on ivan with a SQL editor apply request in question. Ruling R-001 delegated the apply to EXECUTOR, Ivan applied 0001 himself before the ruling landed, and the applied state is now proven in evidence by a full three-phase journal. blocked_on and question are cleared. THE CARD IS FULLY CLOSED.

--- EXECUTOR LOG 2026-08-25 (card shipped) ---
Delivered: supabase/migrations/0001_phase2_schema.sql, one transaction, 108 statements. Eleven tables exactly as listed above, six enum types, three functions, 41 policies, 13 indexes, seven updated_at triggers, and eleven ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY lines, one per table. Acceptance ran green: file present, npx tsc --noEmit exit 0.

DEFAULTS APPLIED (CLAUDE.md section 5, logged rather than asked):
1. UNITS. The unit enum stores the English tokens m2, lm, pcs, bag, kg, roll, m3. Phase 1's lib/mock/types.ts stores the Romanian tokens (buc, sac, rola) directly; the card default says stored enum values are not UI copy, so the English tokens win and the Romanian labels become a presentation-layer lookup. Extended by the same reasoning to inbound_status (pending_arrival, arrived) and outbound_status (awaiting_shipment, shipped), whose phase 1 values are the Romanian display strings.
2. CURRENCY. EUR, RON, MDL per the default. Phase 1's Currency type carried only EUR and RON with a separately stored totalMdl; the card's three-value enum wins and total_mdl stays as a stored column, with no FX and no runtime conversion.
3. SEEDING. units is seeded with all seven rows, because the set is fixed by the enum and an empty units table would leave the product form with nothing to pick. categories is NOT seeded: phase 2 starts with an empty database and no migration from any old system, and phase 1's seven categories were mock data invented for a demo.
4. WRITE RULES. The card default says to fall back to owner-writes when a table's rule is not obvious. Applied to the catalog half: profiles, categories, units and products are owner-write, which is also P2-03's stated rule. NOT applied to the operational half, because that case is not doubtful: inbound_orders, order_lines, batches, outbound_issues, outbound_lines, status_history and reminders are writable by both roles, since P2-04, P2-05 and P2-14 all describe an operator running the daily cycle and P2-02 names exactly one thing the account_manager is refused, which is settings. DELETE on the operational tables stays owner-only. This is the one place the default was deliberately not applied, and it is the first thing to overturn if Ivan disagrees.

JUDGMENT CALLS, all reversible by a later numbered migration:
5. NO SUPPLIERS TABLE. The card's table list is explicit and carries no suppliers table, and adding an unlisted table is scope. Supplier is stored as supplier_name text on products and on inbound_orders, which is what every phase 1 screen that touches a supplier actually reads: a name to display and to filter by. Promoting it to a table is a straightforward migration if the client needs supplier records of their own.
6. THREE COLUMNS ADDED FOR DOWNSTREAM CARDS, all nullable or defaulted, all inside tables the card lists: inbound_orders.document_path and inbound_orders.document_uploaded_at for P2-04's upload, and products.needs_review for P2-09's unmatched-name flag. Each would otherwise force a second migration and a second apply round trip through Ivan.
7. batches.order_line_id CARRIES A UNIQUE CONSTRAINT, which is what makes P2-04's idempotent arrival enforceable by the database rather than by whichever code path happens to run.
8. status_history HAS NO UPDATE AND NO DELETE POLICY, for any role including owner. RLS denies what no policy allows, so append-only is enforced rather than remembered.
9. products HAS NO DELETE POLICY AT ALL, matching P2-03's soft-delete-only default, and the on delete restrict foreign keys back it up.
10. NO STOCK VIEW. Stock is the sum of batches, but the computing view belongs to P2-04, which owns the stock rules. This card creates tables, per its own notes.
11. NO CREATE EXTENSION LINE. gen_random_uuid() has been core since PostgreSQL 13 and every Supabase project runs 15 or later, so a pgcrypto line would add a failure mode for nothing.

VERIFICATION LIMIT, stated plainly: the SQL was never executed. CLAUDE.md section 8 forbids any terminal in this repo from connecting to a database, and there is no local PostgreSQL on this machine. The file was checked by a structural linter that parses the text and executes nothing (scratchpad/lint-migration.mjs, uncommitted): 0 problems, and it confirms eleven tables against eleven RLS lines with every policy, index, trigger and foreign key resolving to a table created in the same file. It cannot catch a syntax error. That is why the file is wrapped in one transaction: a failed apply rolls back whole and costs a round trip, never a partial schema.

--- APPLY VERIFICATION 2026-08-25 (ruling R-001) ---
The apply was verified, not performed, and the difference is recorded rather than smoothed over. The phase 1 pre-check found 11 tables, 6 enums and 41 policies already present. The apply was attempted anyway and failed on 'type app_role already exists', rolling back whole. The phase 3 post-check then confirmed the live schema matches the committed file exactly: 11 tables all with RLS enabled and non-zero policy counts, 6 enums with the exact labels the file declares, both role helpers security_definer, units seeded with 7 rows, and an IDENTICAL table-name diff between file and database. cards.defaults: NO SIGNUP PAGE. Accounts are created by Ivan in the Supabase dashboard and the corresponding profiles row is inserted by hand. A public signup route on an internal warehouse tool is a way in for strangers, not a feature. There is no password reset screen either in this card; Ivan resets from the dashboard. SESSION: use the supabase-js ssr package defaults for cookie handling and refresh. Do not hand-roll refresh timing, do not store tokens in localStorage, do not lengthen the default session lifetime. ROUTE PROTECTION: middleware denies by default and allows an explicit list (the login route, static assets, the auth callback). A new route is protected because it is new, not because someone remembered to add it. ROLE READ: profiles.role is read once per request in middleware and passed down; do not re-query it in every component. UNAUTHENTICATED: redirect to the login route, never render a shell with empty data. AUTHENTICATED BUT WRONG ROLE: a Romanian 403 screen, not a redirect loop and not a silent blank. COPY: all login copy Romanian with diacritics, including the Supabase error strings, which are English by default and must be mapped.

(1) A THRESHOLD OF ZERO IS NOT A THRESHOLD. products.threshold defaults to 0, so every product created without one would email the first time it emptied. That is the second half of this defect and shipping only the first half leaves the operator staring at a button that does nothing. The Supabase browser client has to set the session cookie in the browser, that is P2-02's decided shape, and rewriting it here is scope. DO NOT ADD `method='post'` as the fix: it stops the query-string leak but posts the credentials to a route that does not handle them, which trades a visible defect for a confusing one. cards.title: The Supabase session cookie is written without the Secure attribute.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts` exits 0 with a case added to that file which signs in, reads the browser context cookies, finds the cookie whose name matches /^sb-.*-auth-token/, and asserts `secure === true` and `sameSite === 'Lax'`. The assertion runs against whichever host the suite is pointed at, so it holds in CI and on production alike.
cards.defaults: SET THE COOKIE OPTIONS ON ALL THREE SUPABASE CLIENTS OR ON NONE. The browser client in lib/supabase/client.ts, the server client in lib/supabase/server.ts and the client inside proxy.ts all write the same cookie, so setting `cookieOptions: { secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' }` on one and not the others produces a cookie whose flags depend on which request last wrote it. HTTPONLY STAYS FALSE AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. The @supabase/ssr browser client has to read the session out of the cookie, so httpOnly true would break sign-in; the accepted risk is recorded in docs/reports/critic-wave1.md rather than silently left unexplained. DO NOT SET A CUSTOM COOKIE NAME, DOMAIN OR MAX-AGE. Session lifetime is Supabase's default by P2-02's own defaults and this card does not reopen it. LOCAL DEVELOPMENT MUST KEEP WORKING: `secure` cookies are accepted on http://localhost by every current browser, so no environment switch is needed, and adding one would be the kind of conditional that makes production behave differently from what the tests exercised.
cards.notes:
Read from a real production session with Playwright: the cookie `sb-<ref>-auth-token`, 2577 bytes of token material, is stored with `secure: false`, `httpOnly: false`, `sameSite: 'Lax'` and a persistent expiry. Evidence: critic-wave1/cookies.mjs output. Nothing in the repository sets cookie options; `createBrowserClient` and `createServerClient` are both called with two arguments, so the flags are library defaults. EXPLOITABILITY IS NARROW AND THE FIX IS ONE LINE, which is why this is medium and not high: the site is HTTPS only and answers with `strict-transport-security: max-age=63072000`, so after a browser's first successful visit it will not issue a plain-HTTP request to this host at all. The window is the first-ever visit from a given browser, and any future host or subdomain that is not covered by that HSTS entry. A cookie carrying an access token and a refresh token should carry the flag regardless of how narrow today's window is. NOT RAISED, DELIBERATELY: the absence of CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy on production responses. P2-11 already names security headers in its scope and duplicating it here would split one job across two cards.

All three clients that write the cookie carry the options, from one shared COOKIE_OPTIONS in lib/supabase/cookies.ts: the browser client in lib/supabase/client.ts, the server client in lib/supabase/server.ts and the client inside proxy.ts. httpOnly stays false, and the file says why on its face rather than leaving the next reader to wonder. cards.title: P2-06 acceptance claims dashboard.spec covers an empty database and the manager role, and it covers neither.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/dashboard.spec.ts` exits 0 with the console-and-NaN walk extended so it runs once as owner and once as account_manager over every screen that role can open, and with the empty-state claim either proven or withdrawn. cards.defaults: PREFER PROVING OVER WITHDRAWING, BUT DO NOT FAKE AN EMPTY DATABASE. Truncating tables to reach an empty state is a destructive operation and is forbidden here; the reachable equivalent is a filter that matches nothing, which is what a real operator hits and is what the empty-state markup was written for. IF THE EMPTY-DATABASE CLAIM CANNOT BE PROVEN WITHOUT DESTRUCTIVE SETUP, WITHDRAW IT rather than leaving an acceptance line that describes coverage nobody has. An acceptance that overstates what it checks is worse than a narrower one that is true, because the next reader trusts it. THE MANAGER WALK COVERS ONLY ROUTES THE MANAGER MAY OPEN. /setari answers with the forbidden screen for that role, and asserting no console error on a 403 screen is a real check, so include it and assert the forbidden screen rather than skipping the route. NO PRODUCTION SEEDING. This card runs where the suite already runs.
cards.notes:
P2-06's acceptance line reads: 'dashboard.spec covers the five dashboard blocks against seeded rows, and the same screens against an empty database with no console error and no NaN on screen.' The spec does not do the second half. The console-and-NaN case at tests/e2e/dashboard.spec.ts:125 signs in as owner only, walks the eight screens against whatever the database happens to hold, and asserts no NaN and no console errors. There is no empty-database case and no manager case anywhere in the file. THE EVIDENCE FIELD IS HONEST AND THE ACCEPTANCE FIELD IS NOT, which is the specific shape of this defect and why it is worth a card rather than a shrug: the card's evidence says 'all four stat blocks parse as finite numbers against an arbitrary database state', which is exactly what was run. So nobody lied. The acceptance line was written for a check that was then narrowed, and the two were never reconciled. Per CLAUDE.md section 6 the acceptance is the contract a stranger re-runs, so it has to describe the check that exists. The manager gap matters on its own: the CRITIC sweep is currently the only thing that has ever walked every screen as account_manager looking for console errors, and a wave boundary is not a substitute for a test.

The reachable equivalent, a filter that matches nothing, is what a real operator hits and is what the empty-state markup was written for, so that is what the new case asserts. /setari is kept in the operator walk rather than skipped, per the defaults, and the case asserts the forbidden screen instead of the normal one.
